en.caution: Long-term investors should be cautious about two converging pressures: execution slippage and balance-sheet leverage. The Vineland, New Jersey delay demonstrates that third-party power and permitting bottlenecks can defer revenue even when demand is fully contracted. Meanwhile, scaling CapEx to $40 billion–$45 billion in 2027 while carrying $14.19 billion in debt leaves little margin for error if hyperscaler timelines slip, credit markets tighten, or equity-linked financing resumes and dilutes existing shareholders. Monday’s sharp intraday fade from $110.05 to $97.80 also shows that relief rallies still face heavy overhead selling.
cons: Power-transition delays at DataOne’s Vineland, New Jersey site pushed remaining Microsoft capacity to Q2 2027 and trimmed 2026 revenue guidance.
Capital spending is surging to roughly $27 billion in 2026 and $40 billion–$45 billion in 2027, creating steep execution and funding risk.
Total carrying debt reached $14.19 billion ($16.48 billion principal) on September 30, 2026, alongside a new $3.5 billion Citi credit facility.
Q3 revenue included $325.1 million in non-recurring strategic partnership revenue, and Wall Street banks cut price targets broadly after November 12 earnings.
en.fundamental: Nebius operates in the fast-growing 'neocloud' layer of the AI value chain, deploying dedicated NVIDIA GPU clusters and full-stack cloud software for hyperscalers and AI labs. On November 12, 2026, Q3 results showed rapid scaling: revenue jumped 571% year-over-year to $980.8 million ($973.8 million from Nebius AI Cloud, though $325.1 million was non-recurring partnership revenue), Adjusted EBITDA reached $465.8 million (47.5% margin), and annualized run-rate revenue hit $6.4 billion. However, power-transition delays at a third-party Vineland, New Jersey data center serving Microsoft narrowed FY 2026 revenue guidance toward the low end of $3.0 billion–$3.4 billion while lifting 2026 CapEx to roughly $27 billion. Initial FY 2027 guidance targets $12 billion–$13 billion in revenue and Q4 pre-tax breakeven, but requires $40 billion–$45 billion in CapEx funded via prepayments and asset-backed debt atop $7.43 billion cash and $14.19 billion carrying debt.
en.headline: Nebius Rebounds 20% on Nvidia Catalyst, Yet Execution Delays Weigh on Trend
news: November 23, 2026: NBIS surged 20.28% to $97.80 after NVIDIA’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO following his November 12 resignation, sparking a sector-wide relief rally across NVIDIA-dependent AI clouds.

November 13–16, 2026: Several Wall Street analysts trimmed NBIS price targets after Q3 guidance adjustments, including Citigroup ($265 to $215, Buy), Truist ($355 to $245, Buy), Baird ($340 to $200, Outperform), and DA Davidson ($250 to $125, Neutral).

November 12, 2026: Nebius reported Q3 2026 revenue of $980.8 million (+571% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $465.8 million, while issuing an initial 2027 forecast of $12 billion–$13 billion in revenue and $40 billion–$45 billion in CapEx.

November 12, 2026: Management disclosed third-party power-transition delays at DataOne’s Vineland, New Jersey site serving Microsoft, pushing remaining tranches into Q2 2027 and narrowing FY 2026 revenue guidance to the low end of $3.0 billion–$3.4 billion.

October 22, 2026: Nebius secured a $3.5 billion 364-day senior secured financing facility with Citi to back GPU cluster expansion, following October 16 NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud certification on HGX B300 systems.
en.opportunity: If Nebius delivers its 2027 capacity expansion on schedule, the operating leverage is substantial. Management projects revenue to roughly quadruple from $3.0 billion–$3.2 billion in 2026 to $12 billion–$13 billion in 2027 while reaching pre-tax breakeven by Q4 2027, supported by $38.7 billion in contracted Remaining Performance Obligations. Crucially, advance customer prepayments now cover over 100% of new contracted capacity CapEx ($17 billion–$20 billion expected in 2027), easing balance-sheet strain relative to purely debt-funded neocloud peers and reinforcing Nebius’s tier-one standing with Microsoft, Meta, and NVIDIA.
en.opportunityCheck: The page’s AI-opportunity framework is broadly reasonable on pure-play AI exposure and market growth, but two sub-scores merit adjustment. Market position should move higher: securing a $38.7 billion backlog with Microsoft and Meta, earning NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status on HGX B300, and reaching $6.4 billion in annualized run-rate revenue show Nebius has graduated beyond a tiny early-stage entrant. Conversely, bottleneck and pricing power should edge lower or remain capped; strong customer prepayments help, yet Vineland’s third-party power delays expose real dependence on external colocation operators and NVIDIA hardware supply.
pros: Q3 2026 revenue surged 571% year-over-year to $980.8 million, lifting Adjusted EBITDA to $465.8 million (47.5% margin).
Contracted backlog reached $38.7 billion in Remaining Performance Obligations on September 30, 2026, anchored by Microsoft and Meta deals.
Customer advance prepayments cover over 100% of new contracted capacity CapEx, with $17 billion–$20 billion expected in 2027.
Nebius earned NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status on HGX B300 systems on October 16, 2026, strengthening ties with strategic investor NVIDIA.
risks: Third-party data-center and power-grid bottlenecks (as seen at Vineland, NJ) delaying revenue recognition and straining hyperscaler relationships.
Extreme capital intensity ($40B–$45B 2027 CapEx) requiring uninterrupted customer prepayments, asset-backed financing, and stable credit markets.
Ongoing shareholder dilution risk from convertible notes ($5.75B issued in August 2026) and At-The-Market equity sales funding growth.
High customer and supplier concentration around Microsoft, Meta, and NVIDIA, amplifying volatility around partner spending or governance shocks.
en.summary: Nebius Group (NBIS) surged 20.28% to $97.80 on November 23, 2026 after NVIDIA reinstated CEO Jensen Huang, sparking a relief rally across AI cloud stocks. Even so, NBIS remains in a steep downtrend—67% below its $299.86 52-week high—following its November 12 Q3 report. While Q3 revenue jumped 571% year-over-year to $980.8 million and backlog hit $38.7 billion, Vineland, New Jersey data-center delays trimmed 2026 revenue guidance and a massive $40 billion–$45 billion 2027 capital-spending plan rattled investors. Long-term demand holds, but execution and financing require close watch.
en.technical: NBIS remains in a firm bearish trend despite rallying 20.28% to $97.80 on November 23, 2026. Price sits far below its 50-, 100-, and 200-day exponential moving averages (EMAs, which track average trend prices) at $162.27, $179.45, and $171.28, with the EMA 50 already below the EMA 200—a classic bearish structure. Momentum stays weak: RSI 14 (a 0–100 momentum gauge; under 30 is oversold) bounced only to 36, while MACD (12/26/9, a trend-momentum oscillator) sits at -23.78 below its -21.58 signal line, keeping the histogram negative at -2.21. Volatility is extreme, with Bollinger Bands (20/2, a volatility channel around the 20-day average) stretching from $77.71 to $185.70 and price stuck in the lower half, 67% below the $299.86 52-week high. Volume on November 23 hit 51.69 million shares—1.60 times the 20-day average of 32.26 million—yet price faded from its $110.05 intraday peak to close near the $95.73 session low, signaling heavy overhead supply. Key support sits at $77.71 and the $73.52 52-week low, while $110.05 and the $131.71 Bollinger middle band form initial resistance.

th.summary: หุ้น Nebius Group (NBIS) พุ่ง 20.28% ปิดที่ $97.80 เมื่อวันที่ 23 พ.ย. 2026 หลัง NVIDIA แต่งตั้ง Jensen Huang กลับมาเป็น CEO จุดกระแสรีบาวด์ทั้งกลุ่ม AI Cloud อย่างไรก็ดี ภาพรวม NBIS ยังอยู่ในขาลงรุนแรงและต่ำกว่าจุดสูงสุดรอบ 52 สัปดาห์ที่ $299.86 ถึง 67% หลังงบ Q3 วันที่ 12 พ.ย. แม้งบจะโตร้อนแรง 571% YoY แตะ $980.8 ล้านและมีแบ็กล็อก $38.7 พันล้าน แต่ความล่าช้าของศูนย์ข้อมูลที่ Vineland รัฐนิวเจอร์ซีย์ทำให้ต้องปรับลดกรอบเป้ารายได้ปี 2026 ควบคู่แผนลงทุน CapEx ปี 2027 สูงถึง $40–$45 พันล้าน ฐานอุปสงค์ระยะยาวยังแข็งแกร่ง แต่ต้องจับตาการส่งมอบและการจัดหาเงินทุนใกล้ชิด
th.technical: แม้ NBIS จะดีดตัวแรง 20.28% ปิดที่ $97.80 เมื่อ 23 พ.ย. 2026 แต่โครงสร้างทางเทคนิคยังคงเป็นขาลงชัดเจน ราคาอยู่ต่ำกว่าเส้นค่าเฉลี่ยเคลื่อนที่แบบเอ็กซ์โปเนนเชียล (EMA ซึ่งเป็นเส้นบอกแนวโน้มราคาเฉลี่ย) ทั้ง 50, 100 และ 200 วันที่ $162.27, $179.45 และ $171.28 โดย EMA 50 ตัดลงต่ำกว่า EMA 200 แล้ว สะท้อนแนวโน้มหลักที่เป็นลบ ด้านโมเมนตัมยังอ่อนแอ RSI 14 (ดัชนีวัดแรงซื้อขาย 0–100; ต่ำกว่า 30 คือเขตขายมากเกินไป) ฟื้นขึ้นมาเพียง 36 ขณะที่ MACD (12/26/9 เครื่องมือวัดทิศทางและแรงส่ง) อยู่ที่ -23.78 ต่ำกว่าเส้น Signal ที่ -21.58 ทำให้ Histogram ยังติดลบ -2.21 ความผันผวนสูงมาก กรอบ Bollinger Bands (20/2 ช่องความผันผวนรอบค่าเฉลี่ย 20 วัน) กว้างถึง $77.71–$185.70 โดยราคาอยู่ในครึ่งล่างและต่ำกว่าจุดสูงสุดรอบ 52 สัปดาห์ ($299.86) ถึง 67% แม้ปริมาณซื้อขายวันที่ 23 พ.ย. จะพุ่งถึง 51.69 ล้านหุ้น (1.60 เท่าของค่าเฉลี่ย 20 วันที่ 32.26 ล้านหุ้น) แต่ราคาเปิดกระโดดที่ $110.00 ขึ้นสูงสุด $110.05 แล้วถูกขายกดลงมาปิดใกล้จุดต่ำสุดของวันที่ $95.73 ชี้แรงขายด้านบนยังหนัก แนวรับสำคัญอยู่ที่ $77.71 และจุดต่ำสุดรอบ 52 สัปดาห์ $73.52 ส่วนแนวต้านแรกอยู่ที่ $110.05 และเส้นกลาง Bollinger $131.71
